plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Bidding higher than value risks paying more than the prize is worth if I win with a high second-highest bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $22, the optimal action is to bid exactly $22, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair second-price amount.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy since payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding truthfully ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the competition, and pay less than my value, maximizing expected profit regardless of others' strategies. With a value of $15, I should bid exactly $15 to align my bid with my true valuation, avoiding overbidding (risk of negative profit) or underbidding (missing profitable wins).

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit - bidding higher risks overpaying, bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. With my value at $10, I should bid exactly $10.
